speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 78)
question: What remains in the six-passion range?
premises: In lust-anger-greed-delusion-pride-envy range: intellect uncaused.
That reality remains.
inference: Uncaused within the whole passion-range, reality remains what it was.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 79)
question: What is the world seen as?
premises: Indra-net-made world: cast or picture-work-like.
Whirling, meditating, seeing all: and joy upsurge.
inference: Seen as net and picture-whirl, all-seeing carries joy upsurge.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 80)
question: Where should mind NOT be cast?
premises: Not in pain, not in joy, nor scatter around.
O Bhairavi: in middle what reality remains may be known.
inference: Neither pole — the middle remains, and what remains is knowable.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 81)
question: What happiness comes from leaving body?
premises: Left own-body-standing, everywhere-I-am-thus contemplating.
Firm mind, gaze not seeing else: happy may be.
inference: All-pervading self-contemplation with single gaze makes happy.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 82)
question: What is all-pervading born?
premises: In pot-etc whatever knowing, desire-etc inside me.
Never all-pervading born contemplating: thus all-going.
inference: Contemplating all-pervading born-within, one becomes all-going.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 83)
question: What distinguishes yogins?
premises: Grasper-grasped awareness common of all embodied.
Of yogins but: He is, in relation carefulness.
inference: The yogin's distinction is attentive relation to the common awareness.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 84)
question: What happens in another's body?
premises: Like self in other body: He even awareness should perceive.
Regard of own body left: pervasive in days may be.
inference: Perceiving self in other bodies, regard of one's own dissolves — pervasive.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 85)
question: What happens to thoughts?
premises: Supportless mind made: thoughts not should think.
Then self-supreme-self in: Bhairava, O deer-eyed.
inference: Supportless mind cancels thinking — Bhairava stands in self-supreme-self.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 86)
question: Who am I?
premises: All-knowing, all-doing, pervasive highest-Lord: he indeed I.
Śaiva-natured: thus from firmness Śiva may be.
inference: From firm conviction, 'he indeed I': Śiva-natured one becomes Śiva.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 87)
question: How are the world-plays manifested?
premises: Like water waves, flame-plays of fire, light of sun.
Of me, of Bhairava: these world-plays manifested.
inference: As waves and flames and light, Bhairava's world-plays are only manifestations.
